metadata.name: casino_fair
metadata.description: Provably-fair coin-flip reference program: verifiable randomness via MagicBlock VRF with an authenticated settlement callback.

instructions.name: callback_flip
docs: VRF callback. Invoked by the oracle (never the client). Authenticated by
the `#[vrf_callback]` identity signer, bound to the flip account and to
the `(client_seed, round, requested_slot)` of the request, and
idempotent: a duplicate or stale callback is a no-op.

accounts.name: vrf_program_identity
docs: Scoped VRF identity PDA, bound to this program. Its presence as a signer proves
the callback was issued by the VRF program for this program.

accounts.name: flip
docs: The flip being settled. Re-derived from the player recorded in the
account, so the oracle-supplied account must be the canonical PDA — the
callback cannot be redirected onto a different flip.

instructions.name: cancel_flip
docs: Player-only: abandons an unfulfilled request once
[`CANCEL_TIMEOUT_SLOTS`] have passed since it was made. Bumps the round
so a late callback is ignored. A re-roll vector if stakes are attached.

accounts.name: player
docs: The player. Only the owner of the flip can cancel it.

accounts.name: flip
docs: The player's flip PDA; the seeds bind it to `player`.

instructions.name: close_flip
docs: Player-only: closes the flip account and returns its rent. Refused while
a request is in flight.

accounts.name: player
docs: The player. Receives the account's lamports.

accounts.name: flip
docs: The player's flip PDA; the seeds bind it to `player`. Anchor's `close`
zeroes the data and moves all lamports to `player` after the handler.

instructions.name: init_flip
docs: Creates the caller's singleton `Flip` PDA in the `Idle` state. Run once
per player (again only after `close_flip`).

accounts.name: player
docs: The player. Pays rent for their own flip account and is bound into its
PDA seeds, so one player can never create another player's account.

accounts.name: flip
docs: The player's singleton flip PDA, `["flip", player]`. `init` makes this
run once per player (again only after `close_flip`).

instructions.name: request_flip
docs: Commits `client_seed` and `guess` (0 = HEADS, 1 = TAILS), bumps the
round and asks the VRF oracle for randomness. Rejected while a request
is already in flight — no concurrent flips.

accounts.name: payer
docs: The player, and the payer of the VRF request. Bound into the flip PDA
seeds, so a request can only be made for the signer's own flip.

accounts.name: flip
docs: The player's flip account. `bump = flip.bump` with the player-keyed
seeds ties this account to `payer`: a different signer re-derives a
different PDA and fails the seeds check.

accounts.name: oracle_queue
docs: [`is_allowed_oracle_queue`]: only the base-layer `DEFAULT_QUEUE` unless
the `ephemeral` / `test-queue` cargo features opt in to more.

errors.name: RequestInProgress
errors.msg: A randomness request is already in flight for this player

errors.name: NoRequestInFlight
errors.msg: No randomness request is in flight for this player

errors.name: CancelTooEarly
errors.msg: The cancel timeout has not elapsed yet

errors.name: CloseWhileRequested
errors.msg: Cannot close a flip while a randomness request is in flight

types.name: CoinSide
docs: The two sides of the coin. Stored as a 1-byte enum.
The numeric mapping is part of the client contract: `0 == HEADS`,
`1 == TAILS`. `guess` and `last_result` both use it, so "did the player
win" is a plain equality.

types.name: Flip
docs: Per-player flip account, PDA `["flip", player]`.

fields.name: player
docs: Owner of this flip. The request signer must match it, and the callback
re-derives the PDA from it.

fields.name: status
docs: Lifecycle state. Settlement is only accepted while `Requested`.

fields.name: round
docs: Monotonic request nonce, bumped on every `request_flip` and again on
`cancel_flip`. The callback carries the round it was issued for; a
mismatch means the callback is stale and is ignored.

fields.name: client_seed
docs: Client-chosen byte committed for the live request and echoed back by
the callback. It is a request tag that the callback must match, and it
is folded into the VRF `caller_seed`; at one byte it adds no meaningful
entropy (see the repository's `docs/fairness.md`).

fields.name: guess
docs: The side the player bet on for the live request.

fields.name: bet
docs: Reference-only stake. **Not escrowed by this program.** A real game sets
this when it binds the flip to a `casino_vault` settlement; here it marks
where that binding goes and is left `0`.

fields.name: last_result
docs: Coin side the last settled round landed on. Meaningful once `status` has
reached `Settled` at least once.

fields.name: last_randomness
docs: The exact VRF output the last round was settled with, kept so the result
can be independently re-derived and audited.

fields.name: won
docs: Whether the player won the last settled round (`last_result == guess`).

fields.name: bump
docs: Canonical PDA bump, stored so no instruction re-derives it or accepts a
caller-supplied bump.

fields.name: requested_slot
docs: Slot the live (or most recent) request was made in. Starts the cancel
timeout, and is forwarded to the callback as a second request binding so
a late callback for a cancelled request can never settle a later one —
not even after `close_flip` + `init_flip` restarts `round` at zero.

fields.name: reserved
docs: Zeroed space for future fields, so they can be added without a
reallocation. (Was 64 bytes; 8 went to `requested_slot`, so the account
size is unchanged.)

types.name: FlipCancelledEvent
docs: Emitted by `cancel_flip` when the player abandons an unfulfilled request
after the timeout. No outcome exists for `round`; a late callback for it is
ignored.

fields.name: player
docs: Player whose flip this is.

fields.name: round
docs: The request nonce that was cancelled.

fields.name: requested_slot
docs: Slot the cancelled request was made in.

fields.name: timestamp
docs: Unix timestamp of the enclosing slot.

types.name: FlipRequestedEvent
docs: Emitted by `request_flip` when a randomness request is accepted.
Acceptance is not fulfillment: seeing this event means the oracle was asked,
not that the flip has a result. The matching [`FlipSettledEvent`] (same
`player` + `round`) or [`FlipCancelledEvent`] ends the request.

fields.name: player
docs: Player whose flip this is.

fields.name: round
docs: Request nonce this flip was issued under.

fields.name: guess
docs: Side the player bet on (0 = HEADS, 1 = TAILS).

fields.name: requested_slot
docs: Slot the request was made in; the cancel timeout counts from here.

fields.name: timestamp
docs: Unix timestamp of the enclosing slot.

types.name: FlipSettledEvent
docs: Emitted by `callback_flip` when a round is settled.
Emitted at most once per request: the callback's guard makes a duplicate or
stale delivery a no-op that emits nothing.

fields.name: player
docs: Player whose flip this is.

fields.name: round
docs: Request nonce that was settled; matches the earlier
[`FlipRequestedEvent`].

fields.name: guess
docs: Side the player had bet on.

fields.name: result
docs: Side the verifiable randomness landed on.

fields.name: won
docs: Whether the player won (`result == guess`).

fields.name: timestamp
docs: Unix timestamp of the enclosing slot.

types.name: FlipStatus
docs: Where a flip is in its lifecycle. Stored as a 1-byte enum; new variants are
only ever appended.
```text
Idle ──request──► Requested ──callback──► Settled ──request──► Requested …
└──cancel (after CANCEL_TIMEOUT_SLOTS)──► Cancelled ──request──► …
Only `Requested` accepts a settlement, which is what makes a duplicate or
stale callback a no-op. Every state except `Requested` may be closed.
